extracted.intended_audience: brand drug manufacturers (NDA holders), their counsel, regulatory/compliance officers, and generic manufacturers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how patents may be listed in the FDA Orange Book and the legal/regulatory and antitrust risks of improper listings. Applies to NDA holders submitting patent information and to parties evaluating whether a listing is lawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory listing criteria (21 U.S.C. § 355(b)(1)(A)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: (I) claims the drug for which the applicant submitted the application and is a drug substance (active ingredient) patent or a drug product (formulation or composition) patent; or (II) claims a method of using such drug for which approval is sought or has been granted in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory conditions that must be satisfied for a patent to be submitted for listing in the Orange Book. The Orange Book Transparency Act (2020) codified these requirements. Only patent information submitted under §355(c)(2) is listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting non-required patent information (21 U.S.C. § 355(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Patent information that is not the type of patent information required by subsection (b)(1)(A)(viii) shall not be submitted..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit patents or patent information that fall outside the statutory categories for Orange Book listing. Submitting unrelated or extraneous patent information is expressly forbidden by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-of-use patent listing limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent that is identified as claiming a method of using such drug shall be filed pursuant to section §355(c)(2) for listing in the Orange Book only if the patent claims a method of use approved in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method-of-use patents are listable only when they claim a use that is approved in the NDA (i.e., the specific approved indication/use). Patents claiming unapproved or peripheral uses should not be listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: NDA holder verification and attestation (21 C.F.R. § 314.53(c)(2)(ii)(R); FDA Form 3542)
rubrics_metrics.description: NDA holders are required to submit a signed verification as part of Form FDA 3542 attesting that the submission is an accurate and complete submission of patent information and that the submitter is familiar with 21 C.F.R. 314.53 and that the submission complies with the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation requires an attestation under penalty of perjury. FDA Form 3542 warns that a willfully and knowingly false statement is a criminal offense under 18 U.S.C. §1001. NDA holders must ensure accuracy and completeness before certifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and effects of Orange Book listing (notice and 30‑month stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of listing a patent in the Orange Book is to put potential generic manufacturers on notice that the brand considers the patent to cover its drug. By listing patents, brand drug manufacturers may benefit from a 30-month stay of FDA approval of generic drug applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because listing triggers statutory mechanisms (e.g., paragraph IV litigation rights and the automatic 30‑month stay of ANDA/505(b)(2) approval), NDA holders must exercise care—listing has substantial competitive and regulatory consequences irrespective of the patent’s ultimate validity or scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct or remove improper listings (21 C.F.R. § 314.53(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: NDA holders that currently have patents listed in the Orange Book must ensure that those listings comply with the law and should immediately remove any patents that fail to meet listing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any interested person may request correction of patent information published in the Orange Book under 21 C.F.R. § 314.53(f)(1). Failure to promptly remove improperly listed patents may result in legal liability under the FTC Act or other enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper listing as an unfair method of competition under Section 5 of the FTC Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing patents in the Orange Book that do not meet the statutory listing criteria may constitute an unfair method of competition in violation of Section 5 of the FTC Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FTC treats improper listings as a method of competition (i.e., misuse of regulatory processes) and as unfair when they are not competition on the merits and tend to negatively affect competitive conditions. The Commission will scrutinize listings for these characteristics and may bring enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper listing may support monopolization or use of 'improper means'
rubrics_metrics.description: Improperly listing patents in the Orange Book may constitute an 'improper means' of competition and may be actionable as monopolization where there is willful acquisition or maintenance of monopoly power by improper conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To pursue monopolization claims requires proof of willful acquisition/maintenance of monopoly power via improper conduct. Courts have recognized that Orange Book mislisting can be evidence of 'improper means.' Such conduct may also be relevant in merger review and private antitrust suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual liability and criminal exposure for false certifications or submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who submit or cause the submission of improper Orange Book patent listings, including those who certify compliance under 21 C.F.R. § 314.53(c)(2)(ii)(R), may be held individually liable. False certifications may constitute a potential criminal violation (18 U.S.C. §1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials or employees who sign the required attestation face civil or criminal exposure for false statements; the FTC may refer cases involving false certifications to the Department of Justice. Companies should ensure internal controls to prevent false submissions.
